clue.text: Look up and down all the same

indicators.text: up and down all the same
indicators.note: in a down light the word reads identically whether taken upwards or downwards, so it must be a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Someone glances up and down, and it makes no difference which way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up and down all the same' says the four letters read the same both ways in the grid, a palindrome, and 'Look' supplies the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To peep is to take a quick, furtive glance, a kind of looking.

clue.text: Some are too slow for the city

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the following words are used, signalling a run concealed inside them

explanation.surface: Some people find life too slow to suit the city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes a run of letters from 'tOO SLOw', across the word join; 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway, a city.

clue.text: A traveller in foreign parts must be game!

explanation.surface: An adventurer abroad declares that he is up for anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Marco Polo was the Venetian who journeyed to China; polo is also the mounted sport played with mallets.

clue.text: The action will involve police, that's for certain

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so the action word wraps round the police letters

parts.note: an action is a deed
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: A promise that a police operation is definitely going ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will involve' puts CID inside DEED; 'that's for' links the wordplay to 'certain'.
explanation.definitionFit: Decided as an adjective means definite or settled, beyond doubt.

clue.text: Guy the agent is a lawbreaker

parts.note: a guy is a man, a male
a factor is an agent acting for someone, such as an estate manager

explanation.surface: A man described as an agent turns out to be a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a name (Guy Fawkes, fittingly a lawbreaker) but just means a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a wrongdoer, someone who commits a crime.

clue.text: Prison seen differently by old people

indicators.note: the letters are seen in a different arrangement, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Elderly folk view a jail in a new light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'differently' rearranges the ten letters of PRISON SEEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensioners are retired people drawing a pension, typically elderly.

clue.text: Make a song about subordinate being cutting

indicators.note: the singing word goes around, containing the subordinate word

parts.note: to make a song is to sing
under means lower in rank, subordinate

explanation.surface: Someone composes a tune about a junior employee being sharp-tongued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts UNDER inside SING; 'being' is a link and 'cutting' the definition, not a description of the subordinate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundering is splitting apart, severing, the action of cutting.

clue.text: Writing a feature on soft fruit

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft
an ear is a feature of the head

explanation.surface: Penning a piece about soft fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' sets EAR after P in this across light; 'Writing' plays no part in the wordplay as held.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a tree fruit with a tapering shape.

clue.text: A top man's pride sent crashing

indicators.note: the letters are sent crashing into disorder, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A head of state's self-esteem is brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' rearranges PRIDE SENT; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a republic or organisation, a leading figure.

clue.text: Professional mobility being given encouragement

parts.note: pro is short for professional
motion is movement, mobility

explanation.surface: An expert on the move is cheered on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being given' links the wordplay to 'encouragement'.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotion means furthering or advancing something, actively supporting it.

clue.text: Answered so were introduced

explanation.surface: A reply given, and so two people got to know each other.
explanation.definitionFit: To have met a demand is to have satisfied or responded to it; people who met were brought together for the first time.

clue.text: Continually setting a girl right

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone forever putting a young woman straight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means always, at all times.

clue.text: The underworld boss is after a key

indicators.note: the word is comes after the key letter in the answer

parts.note: D is a musical key

explanation.surface: A gangland chief wants something unlocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The underworld boss' sounds like a mob leader but is the Roman god ruling the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Dis is the Roman god of the dead, ruler of the realm below.

clue.text: A crawler will get pie-decent pie

indicators.note: pie is printer's term for jumbled type, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A creeping creature is promised a pie that is quite good.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'pie' is the printer's word for type jumbled together, so it signals an anagram of PIEDECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A centipede is a many-legged arthropod that creeps along the ground.

clue.text: A caucus to learn about on opening one

indicators.note: the two short words go around the opening and the one

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
taken as written
a vent is an opening
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A political meeting to study something to do with the opening of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts VENT and I between CON and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A convention is a formal assembly of delegates, like a party meeting.

clue.text: For recording music?

parts.note: read as books in which musical notes are written down, rather than recording equipment

explanation.surface: Asking what equipment captures music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recording' suggests tapes and studios, but the items are books for writing in.
explanation.definitionFit: Notebooks are small books for jotting things down.

clue.text: Island where people are accommodated without charge

parts.note: an inn is where guests are put up
something without charge is free, read here as the statement 'is free'

explanation.surface: An island where lodging costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as the sentence 'inn is free'. Innisfree is a small island in Lough Gill, Ireland, made famous by Yeats.
explanation.definitionFit: Innisfree is a small lake isle in County Sligo, Ireland.

clue.text: A painter stays inside in this country

indicators.note: the painter remains within the word in, a container

parts.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: An artist stays put in this land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stays inside' puts RA inside IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Iran is a nation in western Asia.

clue.text: The favoured way a worker gets tick

parts.note: to be in is to be in favour
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
a worker ant is the stock crossword worker

explanation.surface: A favourite route for an employee earns a mark of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tick' is not a check mark but the British sense of a moment, as in 'just a tick'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tick is a very short time, a moment, which is what instant means as a noun.

clue.text: Some fiction should be about animals, it's ruled

indicators.note: the fiction word goes around the animals word

parts.note: a lie is a piece of fiction
neat is an old word for cattle

explanation.surface: Stories about animals are said to be the rule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'should be about' puts NEAT, old word for cattle, inside LIE; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineate means marked with lines, as ruled paper is.

clue.text: Criticise the Left and find understanding

parts.note: to rap is to rebuke or criticise
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: Attack the political Left and you will find common ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Left' suggests politics but is the nautical left, PORT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapport is a close, harmonious relationship of mutual understanding.

clue.text: Simple, in Father Brown's opinion

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Simple, in Father Brown's opinion': 'Simple' defines HERB (a medicinal plant), but no reading of 'in Father Brown's opinion' gives HERB, and no other print was found.

clue.text: Crime perpetrated by real thugs

indicators.note: the crime is worked by these words, so their letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An offence committed by genuine ruffians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perpetrated by' reworks REAL THUGS into the crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Slaughter is killing, especially mass killing, a serious offence.

clue.text: Keeps within reach, as often needed

indicators.note: the letters lie within the words that follow, across the join

explanation.surface: Someone keeps things handy, since they are often wanted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' takes the run from 'reacH AS'; 'often needed' completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To have something is to keep or hold it.

clue.text: Concerned with restraining a lout

indicators.note: the word for concerned with holds the letter in, as a container

parts.note: of can mean about or concerning, as in 'talk of war'

explanation.surface: Someone involved in holding back a thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restraining' puts A inside OF.
explanation.definitionFit: An oaf is a clumsy, boorish person, much like a lout.

clue.text: A German races in circles

indicators.note: the races letters sit inside the two circles

parts.note: O is shaped like a circle, so two circles give two Os
TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A German driver goes round and round the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts TT inside OO; TT is the Isle of Man Tourist Trophy motorbike races.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German man's name.

clue.text: Put down the newspapers to cut the long grass

indicators.note: the newspapers word cuts into the grass word, splitting it

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
the press is the newspapers collectively

explanation.surface: Lay down newspapers before mowing the tall grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' puts PRESS inside REED.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress a rebellion is to crush or quell it, to put it down.

clue.text: A nymph's sound reflection

explanation.surface: A nymph's sound, reflected back.
explanation.definitionFit: Echo is the Greek nymph who pined for Narcissus; an echo is also a reflected sound.

clue.text: The best mounted notice

indicators.note: in a down light, mounted means going up, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: tops means the very best

explanation.surface: The finest framed poster on the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounted' turns TOPS upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot is to notice or catch sight of.

clue.text: A lady made to change her make-up

indicators.note: changing the make-up, the composition, of the word made rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: A woman is forced to redo her cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' suggests cosmetics but means the letters' composition, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A dame is a woman, especially a titled lady or an older woman.

clue.text: See craft result in defeat

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning see or behold
SS is the abbreviation for steamship, a craft

explanation.surface: Watch the boat end up beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'result in' links the wordplay to 'defeat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss is a defeat in a contest.

clue.text: The marrow's adversely affected by creatures in the soil

indicators.note: the letters are damaged out of shape, signalling an anagram

parts.note: taken letter for letter, including the s

explanation.surface: A gardener's marrow is damaged by pests underground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adversely affected' rearranges THE MARROWS, the s included.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthworms are burrowing worms living in soil.
